answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that grows with the privileges it claims. Creating one identity is cheap, but spawning thousands becomes expensive because every copy must post its own bond, and misbehavior slashes it. Reputation then accrues slowly through verified work: trust forms like jade polished over time, while a ferrous backbone of audited task history makes fakes easy to spot, and copper traces of real payments tie activity to scarce resources. Attackers pay per identity, so flooding the network stops paying off.
